bugs.creator: michaelchirico4
bugs.summary: tapply() fails to combine attributes correctly (difftime)

comments.creator: michaelchirico4
comments.text:
```
t <- .POSIXct(c(0, 1, 0, 3*60*60))
g <-          c(1, 1, 2,       2))

tapply(t, g, diff)
# 1 2 
# 1 3 

tapply(t, g, \(x) x[2] - x[1]) # same

# c.difftime exists and does the right thing!
c(diff(t[g==1]), diff(t[g==2]))
# Time differences in secs
# [1]     1 10800
```

I don't see anything about attributes mentioned in `?tapply`.

data.table does _slightly_ better:

```
data.table(t, g)[, diff(t), by=g]
#        g         V1
#    <num> <difftime>
# 1:     1     1 secs
# 2:     2     3 secs

data.table(t, g)[, t[2]-t[1], by=g]
#        g         V1
#    <num> <difftime>
# 1:     1     1 secs
# 2:     2 10800 secs
```

dplyr handles this pretty well:

```
summarize(data.frame(t, g), diff(t), .by="g")
#   g    diff(t)
# 1 1     1 secs
# 2 2 10800 secs

summarize(data.frame(t, g), t[2]-t[1], .by="g")
#   g t[2] - t[1]
# 1 1      1 secs
# 2 2  10800 secs
```

Just saw r84928 which helps here by exposing `units=` to `diff()`, great!

```
tapply(t, g, diff, units='secs')
#     1     2 
#     1 10800

data.table(t, g)[, diff(t, units='secs'), by=g]
#        g         V1
#    <num> <difftime>
# 1:     1     1 secs
# 2:     2 10800 secs
```

I still think `tapply()` is doing the wrong thing here by missing the `c()` method dispatch; e.g. the natural-looking `t[2]-t[1]` has no way to specify `units=` and winds up garbled/incorrect.
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
Poking a little more: `simplify=FALSE` (obviously) doesn't have this issue; it's the `unlist()` step where the attributes get mangled. So at root this is about:

```
unlist(list(
  as.difftime(1, units='secs'),
  as.difftime(1, units='hours')))
# [1] 1 1
```

`?unlist` also doesn't mention anything about attributes, and I don't see any related issue on the tracker, so leaving this open as is.
comments.creator: michaelchirico4

comments.text:
I think you want 'simplify = FALSE':

R> t <- .POSIXct(c(0, 1, 0, 3*60*60))
g <-          c(1, 1, 2,       2)
tapply(t, g, diff, simplify = FALSE)
$`1`
Time difference of 1 secs

$`2`
Time difference of 3 hours

By default, tapply simplifies to array in the all-length-one case, which necessarily drops classes.
comments.creator: Kurt.Hornik
michaelchirico4
comments.text:
> which necessarily drops classes.

The proposed patch avoids that by using `c()` instead of `unlist()`:

https://github.com/r-devel/r-svn/pull/183/files

The question is whether that's a substantially better default, or whether the caller should do that on their own with `simplify=FALSE`.

(I haven't added the patch here yet since I haven't given it enough testing)
